explanations: post sorts the account ids but does not dedupe them. AccountLock is not reentrant, so when a journal has two postings on the same account the loop acquires that account's lock, then awaits it again and waits on itself forever. transfer with a non-zero fee always does this (fromId appears for the principal and the fee), so every fee-bearing transfer hangs, and the stuck lock also blocks every later operation on that account. The fix is `[...new Set(postings.map((p) => p.accountId))].sort()`.

A global acquisition order prevents the classic A-waits-for-B, B-waits-for-A deadlock between concurrent transfers in opposite directions. append receives the original postings array (unsorted), Map iteration is insertion order and unrelated, and sorting does nothing for Map lookups.

The check aggregates postings per account into `net` first, so A's delta is -500 + 300 = -200, and 250 + (-200) = 50 is not negative. Individual postings are never checked alone, positive deltas are skipped with continue, and balancing only gates the earlier UnbalancedJournalError.

Every lock acquired is pushed to `held`, and the finally block releases all of them in reverse order whatever the error type. The table keeps locks forever but that has no bearing on release, and there is no error-type check.
